question.prompt: After \(\triangle ABC\) is translated, \(A(-1,2)\) corresponds to \(A'(3,5)\), and point \(B\) corresponds to \(B'(6,1)\). Find the coordinates of point \(B\). (Enter the horizontal coordinate first, then the vertical coordinate, separated by a comma.)

solutions.explanation: \(A\to A'\) is a translation 4 units to the right and 3 units upward, so the coordinates of \(B\) are obtained by translating \(B'\) in the reverse direction: \((6-4,1-3)=(2,-2)\).
solutions.title: Reverse the translation
